title: No integer lies strictly between zero and one
statement: There is no integer x with 0 < x and x < 1.

formal.statement: theorem Int.no_int_between : ((x0 : Int) -> Not (And (Int.lt Int.zero x0) (Int.lt x0 Int.one)))

evidence.supports: There is no integer x with 0 < x and x < 1.
evidence.notes: `build_int_prelude` admits this theorem through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type, so a green run of the command is a machine-checked proof. Measured 2026-08-14: 12 tests pass (a nonzero count -- the filter is not inert).

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- this theorem's trusted closure is empty
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example int_theorem_inventory -- no_int_between 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^theorem[[:space:]]+Int\.no_int_between[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: Two independent bounds, because either alone would be weaker than it looks. (1) `Kernel::axiom_footprint` walks THIS declaration's transitive dependencies and prints an empty footprint column -- this is the kernel's `#print axioms`, and it is the check that matters, since an integer law IS still asserted (`Int.euclidean_decomposition`; it was 6 until lane int-remainder proved the `subNatNat` borrow, and the check mattered more then) and Int.no_int_between could have reached for one and still type-checked. (2) `nat_axiom_inventory` reports `nat: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0` for the development ZZ is constructed over, so the foundation admits no trusted declaration at all. Counting `Declaration::Axiom` alone would not have sufficed: `Opaque` has no proof body and `Quotient` admits `Quot.sound`, which is exactly the declaration the quotient-of-NxN construction would have added -- the enumeration covers all three kinds and reports zero for each.

evidence.supports: the theorem is usable as a refutation, not merely well-typed
evidence.notes: Applies the theorem to an abstract `x : Int` and a conjunction built from hypotheses `0 < x` and `x < 1`, then `infer`s the result and checks it is definitionally `False`. This is the step the Diophantine refutation route actually performs.

provenance.source: one of the 34 propositions build_int_prelude previously ASSERTED; this lane constructed ZZ over the proved Nat development and derived it

notes: This is the integer-specific fact the ordered field RR lacks, and the one an integer-cut / Diophantine refutation invokes to kill a residue g*m = r with 0 < r < g. It was previously the headline ASSUMPTION of the integer route; it is now derived. The proof splits x on its constructor: for `Int.negSucc n` the hypothesis `0 < x` itself reduces to `False`, and for `Int.ofNat n` the two bounds reduce to `1 <= n` and `n+1 <= 1`, which chain through `Nat.le_of_succ_le_succ`, `Nat.le_trans` and `Nat.not_succ_le_zero` to a contradiction. Those three Nat theorems are not themselves in this ledger; all are axiom-free (`nat_axiom_inventory` reports zero trusted declarations for the whole Nat environment). formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, verbatim from `int_theorem_inventory`.
